meta.title: Colorado local housing funds, dedicated taxes, linkage fees, land and ownership tools
meta.method: Curated, not a feed. Each record was read from the jurisdiction's own code, ordinance, ballot question or election result, budget or program page, the text saved, and every evidence quote checked by exact substring match against the saved text (whitespace normalised). verification.level "primary" means read from that official document; "reported" means taken from a named outlet without the primary document, and verification.by names it. Every dollar figure and percentage a record states appears in its own evidence quotes (tests/test_local_incentives.py). A figure the source does not publish is null, never 0. Fee relief and land-use incentives are in data/policy/fee-reductions.json, not here.
meta.review_rule: review_by is about 90 days out for records that change yearly (fund balances, program pages) and about six months for code- or ballot-backed records. policy-review-reminders.yml opens an issue a week before a record is due; the page shows a warning once it is overdue.
known_gaps: Coverage is partial: see data/policy/incentive-coverage.json for who has been checked. A jurisdiction with no record has not been shown to have no fund or tax.
Annual revenue is recorded only where the source states it; most records leave it null.

entries.uses: development, acquisition, preservation and operation of for-sale and rental homes for low/moderate-income households and local workforce; housing-stability services; grants to housing authorities, nonprofits and municipalities
entries.summary: Boulder County voters in 2023 (83,505 to 33,426) extended the existing 0.185% sales and use tax for fifteen years, through 2039, to fund affordable and attainable housing; the county projected $16.7 million in revenue for 2025.
entries.authorizing_code: Boulder County BOCC Resolution 2023-070; County Issue 1B (Nov. 7, 2023)

source.label: Boulder County Resolution 2023-070 and 2023 Coordinated Election results

verification.against: Resolution 2023-070; Boulder County 2023 Coordinated Election results (electionresults.bouldercounty.gov/ElectionResults2023C/); bouldercounty.gov AAHT pages

evidence.quote: Boulder County Ballot Issue 1B Affordable and Attainable Sales and Use Tax Extension and Revenue Change Candidate Votes Percent 1513 82 73 Yes/For 83,505 83505 1514 83 74 No/Against 33,426 33426

Beginning January 1, 2025, the net proceeds from the 0.185% countywide sales and use tax received by the County shall be expended by the County for the purposes of funding affordable and attainable housing and related support services
The sales and use tax described in this Resolution expires on December 31, 2039.
Boulder County voters overwhelmingly approved the tax in 2023 and the AAHT is projected to provide $16.7 million in revenue in 2025.

evidence.section: Affordable and Attainable Housing Tax page
evidence.quote: In the 2023 General Election, Boulder County voters approved an extension of an existing .185% sales and use tax with 71% support.

entries.notes: Rate was previously dedicated to jail/alternative sentencing (Res. 2018-76) through 2024; housing use began Jan. 1, 2025. annual_revenue left null because the $16.7M figure is a projection. Initial allocation per county release: about 65% ($9.7m) development, 35% ($5m) supportive services, $500,000 innovation grants; development money split 30% Longmont, 32% Boulder, 38% rest of county. Also note a separate 0.05% health and human services sales tax (2017 extension to 2033) can fund capital for housing authorities; not recorded here because that page (2017 ballot issues) returned 404.

source.label: Adams County Housing Policy & Community Investments page

verification.against: Adams County Housing Policy & Community Investments page

evidence.section: NOTICE: Rights to Property for Affordable Housing Law Notice
evidence.quote: As of November 11, the Adams County Board of Commissioner has opted to retain its Right of First Offer (ROFO) and universally assign its Right of First Refusal to Maiker Housing Partners.
As of August 7, 2024, the Local Government Rights to Property for Affordable Housing law (HB24-1175) is in effect.

entries.uses: Rental production/preservation and rental assistance (<=80% AMI), for-sale housing (<=100% AMI), homebuyer assistance (<=120% AMI), supportive housing and anti-displacement programs
entries.summary: Denver's affordable housing permanent funds receive linkage-fee revenue and a dedicated property tax levy plus a share of retail marijuana sales tax, and may be spent only on income-restricted housing programs, with administration capped at 8 percent.

source.label: Denver Revised Municipal Code ch. 27, art. V (Municode API)

verification.against: Denver Revised Municipal Code 27-150 (Municode API)

evidence.quote: The affordable housing permanent funds shall consist of the Affordable Housing Linkage Fee Revenue Fund created for the exclusive purpose of receiving and accounting for all revenues derived from the affordable housing linkage fees
For the production or preservation of rental housing, including the funding of rental assistance programs, for qualified households earning eighty (80) percent or less of AMI.
For the production or preservation of for-sale housing for qualified households earning one hundred (100) percent or less of AMI.
For homebuyer assistance programs, including by way of example down payment and mortgage assistance programs, for qualified households earning one hundred and twenty (120) percent or less of AMI.

in no event shall the amount expended from the funds for such administrative expenses in any year exceed eight (8) percent of the amount of revenue received in the Affordable Housing Linkage Fee Revenue Fund that year

entries.notes: Two funds under one article: the Affordable Housing Linkage Fee Revenue Fund and the Affordable Housing Property Tax and Other Local Revenue Fund. Annual revenue is not stated in the code. The former Division 4 sunset provision (27-170) now reads 'Reserved'. Separate records cover the levy, the marijuana tax share and the linkage fee.

entries.rate_text: $1.75-$9.00 per sq ft of GFA by use (July 2022-July 2025 schedule), CPI-adjusted from July 1, 2026
entries.uses: Rental and for-sale housing and homebuyer assistance for households at or below 80% AMI
entries.summary: Denver charges an affordable housing linkage fee per square foot of new floor area, phased up to $5.00 (small dwellings) through $9.00 (commercial uses in high market areas) by July 2025 and indexed to CPI from July 2026; residential projects may instead comply with mandatory affordable housing.

source.label: Denver Revised Municipal Code ch. 27, art. V (Municode API)

verification.against: Denver Revised Municipal Code 27-153 (Municode API)

evidence.quote: an affordable housing linkage fee shall be imposed prior to the issuance of a building permit for any new structure or for any addition to an existing structure that increases the gross floor area

Dwelling unit(s) of 1,600 square feet or less of GFA within a single-unit dwelling, two-unit dwelling, or multi-unit dwelling or live/work dwelling of 9 dwelling units or less. $1.75 $2.83 $3.92 $5.00

Any primary commercial sales services and repair uses or any primary civic, public or institutional uses in a high market area as high market area is defined in section 27-219 . $3.65 $5.43 $7.22 $9.00
To increase the supply of affordable rental housing, including the funding of renter assistance programs, for qualified households earning eighty (80) percent or less of AMI

entries.notes: Columns are effective July 1 of 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025. Other rows: >1,600 sf dwellings $8.00; other primary residential $7.00; commercial typical market $6.00; industrial/agricultural $2.50 (2025 column). Exceptions in 27-154. The fee now applies mainly where Article X (mandatory affordable housing) does not; 27-153(c) lets residential applicants comply with Article X instead.

entries.rate_text: $250,000-$478,000 per required income-restricted unit (2022 base), CPI-adjusted annually
entries.uses: First offsets the EHA building-permit fee reduction; remainder for rental (<=80% AMI), for-sale (<=100% AMI) and homebuyer assistance (<=120% AMI)
entries.summary: Under Expanding Housing Affordability, Denver developers may pay a fee in lieu per required income-restricted unit ($311,000 rental / $478,000 ownership in high market areas; $250,000-$408,000 in typical areas) into the Mandatory Affordable Housing Special Revenue Fund.

source.label: Denver Revised Municipal Code ch. 27, art. V (Municode API)

verification.against: Denver Revised Municipal Code 27-220 and 27-225 (Municode API)

evidence.quote: An applicant may satisfy its requirements under this division by making a fee-in-lieu payment that will be deposited in the Mandatory Affordable Housing Revenue Fund.

High Market Area 10% of dwelling units Rental development $311,000.00 Ownership development $478,000.00 Typical Market Area 8% of total dwelling units Townhouses $250,000.00 Ownership development, dwelling units other than townhouses $408,000.00

(1) For the production or preservation of rental housing, including the funding of rental assistance programs, for qualified households earning eighty (80) percent or less of AMI. (2) For the production or preservation of for-sale housing for qualified households earning one hundred (100) percent or less of AMI. (3) For homebuyer assistance programs, including by way of example, down payment and mortgage assistance programs, for qualified households earning one hundred twenty (120) percent or less of AMI.

The director shall use the Mandatory Affordable Housing Special Revenue Fund for the primary purpose of offsetting the costs of the building permit fee reduction incentive provided in section 27-224 .

entries.notes: Typical-market rental: $250,000 (1-7 stories) and $295,000 (8+ stories). Amounts are the codified 2022 base; CPI-U adjusted each July 1 from 2023 via a CPD schedule not read here. The inclusionary requirement itself is already in fee-reductions.json (denver-eha-inclusionary-requirement).

entries.uses: Affordable housing (proposed)
entries.summary: Denver voters narrowly rejected Ballot Issue 2R in November 2024, which would have raised the city sales tax by 0.5 points for affordable housing.

source.label: Colorado Politics, 'Denver Mayor Mike Johnston cedes affordable housing ballot loss' (2024-11-11)

verification.against: Colorado Politics (news report); Denver Elections official results page not fetched
verification.by: Colorado Politics (news report); Denver Elections official results page not fetched

evidence.quote: But on Saturday, Johnston conceded Ballot Issue 2R’s failure, which lost at the ballot box by a slim margin.
His funding proposal this year — which would have raised the city’s sales tax rate by 0.5 points— would have cost roughly $30 million more than his campaign pitch.
As of Monday, 50.74% of voters said “no.”

entries.notes: Reported, not primary; the 50.74% 'no' figure was a partial count as of the article date. The brief's 'Initiated Ordinance 305 (2022)' is a different measure: per news coverage it was a $75/unit landlord fee for eviction legal defense, which failed; it was not a housing fund and is not recorded.

entries.uses: Build, rehabilitate or acquire affordable housing; administration of inclusionary programs

verification.against: Boulder Revised Code 9-13-10 and City of Boulder affordable housing investments page

entries.uses: Increase the supply of affordable housing for working households

entries.uses: Acquire, hold and sell land to housing providers for affordable rental (<=60% AMI) and ownership (<=80% AMI) housing
entries.summary: Fort Collins's land bank buys land near transit, schools, parks, jobs and shopping, paid from the Affordable Housing Fund or General Fund, and sells it only to housing providers bound to build rentals for households at or below 60 percent of AMI or ownership homes at or below 80 percent.
entries.authorizing_code: Fort Collins Municipal Code 23-350 to 23-354 (Ord. No. 48, 2001; Ord. No. 037, 2018)

source.label: Fort Collins Municipal Code ch. 23, art. XIII Land Banking (Municode API)

verification.against: Fort Collins Municipal Code 23-350-23-354 (Municode API)

evidence.quote: The purpose of this Article is to enable the City to acquire, hold and sell real property to assist housing providers (whether publicly affiliated, philanthropic or profit-motivated) in providing affordable rental and homeownership housing.
The acquisition of land pursuant to this Article shall be funded from the Affordable Housing Fund, the General Fund, or other available funding source.
a. Rental housing shall be restricted to households at or below sixty (60) percent of AMI. b. Homeownership housing shall be restricted to households at or below eighty (80) percent of AMI.

entries.notes: Number of parcels held is not in the code; fcgov.com program pages returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch. The code references an 'Affordable Housing Fund' but no code section creating it was found in ch. 8 art. III (funds), so no separate housing_trust_fund record.

entries.uses: Affordable housing programs and services

entries.uses: Competitive gap-financing loans to build and rehabilitate affordable housing in Arvada
entries.summary: The Arvada Housing Authority manages the Arvada Affordable Housing Fund, which makes competitive gap-financing loans for affordable housing construction and rehabilitation; the 2024 Housing Strategic Plan calls for giving it a dedicated revenue source.

source.label: City of Arvada, Affordable Housing in Arvada

verification.against: City of Arvada Affordable Housing in Arvada page and 2024 Housing Strategic Plan page

evidence.quote: Arvada Affordable Housing Fund: The Arvada Housing Authority manages a fund to provide gap financing loans to upcoming construction projects in Arvada.
The Arvada Affordable Housing Fund is a gap financing source available to housing developers looking to build and rehabilitate projects in Arvada.
Create a dedicated, sustainable revenue source to fund the Arvada Affordable Housing Fund (AAHF).

entries.notes: arvadaco.gov returns HTTP 403 to automated fetch; text read from the city's own CivicPlus host (co-arvada.civicplus.com). No dedicated revenue source as of the plan (adopted May 20, 2024). The plan also lists 'Continue to allocate publicly owned land (and/or acquire properties) for affordable and mixed-income housing' as a strategy; not recorded as a program because no program terms were found. Creation date and size not stated.
